subject: Re: Proxima Bank escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception
body:
From: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception
Attachments: proxima-429-samples-20260118.txt

Hi Neha,

We’re seeing a material increase in 429s since late last week on our production traffic. This is impacting a customer-facing workflow around market open.

Details:
- Route(s): /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings
- Region: us-east
- Window: 09:30–09:45 ET (peak)
- Pattern: bursts of ~8–10 minutes, then back to baseline
- What we see: HTTP 429 with Retry-After values between 1–5 seconds

We need a temporary burst exception while we rework our client-side batching and backoff. Can you help raise our burst allowance for the next few weeks?

We’ve attached a small sample of responses with headers.

Thanks,
Daniel

—
Daniel Weber
Director, AI Platform
Proxima Bank



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Cc: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception
Attachments: redwood-overload-protection-headers-and-retry-guidance-v1.pdf, screenshot-us-east-overload-dashboard-20260118.png

Hi Daniel,

Thanks for flagging (and for including the header samples).

What changed:
We enabled our “hot-route capacity protection” controls in us-east for the top traffic routes. The goal is to prevent a small number of bursty workloads from pushing shared pools into tail-latency/5xx events. The behavior you’re seeing is consistent with the new tier-aware admission control.

What we see on our side for Proxima (us-east):
- During 09:30–09:44 ET on Jan 17, the region entered a sustained pressure state on the chat and embeddings pools.
- Your traffic saw 429s primarily with reason “overload_shed” (as opposed to “quota_exceeded”).
- For your enterprise tier class, latency SLO stayed within target; the 429s were driven by burst admission controls (to keep the pool stable) rather than an outage.

Key headers to look at (also in the attached one-pager):
- Retry-After: seconds
- x-redwood-throttle-reason: overload_shed | quota_exceeded
- x-redwood-priority-class: enterprise | best_effort

On the ask for a temporary burst exception:
Yes, we can approve a time-bounded burst increase with guardrails.

Proposed temporary exception (starting Jan 21):
- Account: Proxima Bank
- Region: us-east
- Routes: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings
- Burst increase: +75% above current burst cap
- Constraints/guardrails:
  1) Auto-expire on Feb 15 (unless renewed)
  2) Must honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff + jitter
  3) If shed rate for your tenant exceeds 5% for >5 minutes OR enterprise p95 breaches threshold for 10 minutes, we roll back to default to protect the fleet
  4) No change to monthly quota; this is strictly burst/headroom behavior

Two quick questions so we set this correctly:
1) Is the burst primarily embeddings, chat, or both?
2) Typical request shape during the burst (approx prompt tokens + max output tokens for chat; dimensions/model for embeddings)?

If you can reply with those, I’ll get the config queued for the next change window.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Executive Sponsor, Reliability
Redwood Inference



From: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Hi Neha,

Thanks. This is helpful.

To your questions:
1) Both, but embeddings is the bigger spike (roughly 2:1 vs chat)
2) Shapes:
- embeddings: ~800–1200 input tokens, 1024-dim, model “r-embed-large” (per your catalog)
- chat: prompt typically 1.5–2k tokens, max_output_tokens=256, streaming enabled

We can implement stricter Retry-After honoring on our end this week.

What burst cap are we talking about in RPS terms? Our peak hits closer to 450 RPS combined.

Sonia



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Cc: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Sonia (cc Daniel),

Got it — thank you.

On RPS: your current configured burst ceiling (account-level, us-east) is 260 RPS combined across those two routes with a short burst window; the protection system starts applying backpressure when the pool pressure signal is sustained.

Given your peak closer to ~450 RPS combined, I’m not comfortable taking you straight to 450 in a shared pool without additional constraints.

Counterproposal (still temporary, with strict guardrails):
- New burst ceiling: 400 RPS combined
- Burst window: 120 seconds (requires backoff compliance; otherwise you’ll get oscillations)
- Additional request-shape guardrail for chat during the burst window:
  - max_output_tokens <= 256 (as you already do)
  - if prompt tokens exceed ~3k, we may still shed those requests first under pressure

We’ll also tag this as “temporary_exception=true” in decision logs so Support/SRE can identify it quickly during an incident.

If you confirm 400 RPS works, I’ll proceed.

Neha



From: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 10:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Neha,

400 RPS should be workable as an interim step.

Two follow-ups:
1) Can we scope it specifically to the 09:25–09:50 ET window to reduce risk?
2) If we still see 429s, do you have a recommended retry strategy beyond obeying Retry-After? (We’re currently doing fixed 1s retries; we can change.)

Daniel



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Cc: Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 11:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Daniel,

1) Yes — we can scope the exception to a time window. We’ll implement a scheduled policy: 09:25–09:50 ET weekdays, us-east, for the two routes, with the 400 RPS ceiling.

2) Retry strategy:
- Treat Retry-After as authoritative (don’t retry sooner)
- Use exponential backoff with jitter on top (e.g., base 250–500ms, cap at 5s) for “overload_shed”
- For “quota_exceeded”, retrying in a tight loop won’t help; you’ll need to wait for the next quota window
- For streaming chat: if the connection is terminated due to shedding, re-issue with a new request id and the same payload only if your application semantics allow. (Avoid aggressive immediate replays.)

Also: fixed 1s retries across the whole burst tends to synchronize and can amplify load. Jitter is important.

Ava (cc’d) is tracking exec-level escalations and will be aware of the temporary exception and expiry date.

Next steps (on our side):
- I’ll have the team implement the scheduled exception effective Wed Jan 21
- We’ll monitor shed rate + p95 for your tenant during the window and share a brief report after the first two market opens

Please confirm:
- The window is ET (09:25–09:50)
- You’re OK with the Feb 15 auto-expiry

Neha



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 11:23 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Daniel,

Jumping in briefly — we’ll treat this as a temporary reliability exception with an explicit end date and will proactively follow up a week before expiry.

If you can share (even rough) expected peak RPS for the next 4 weeks, that will help us avoid surprises.

Thanks,
Ava

Ava Chen
Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference



From: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 11:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Confirmed:
- Time window in ET (09:25–09:50)
- Feb 15 auto-expiry is fine

Expected peaks (next 4 weeks):
- Typical: 420–450 RPS combined at open
- End-of-month: could hit 480 RPS for 2–3 days

We’ll deploy jittered exponential backoff and enforce Retry-After by end of week.

Thanks for moving quickly.
Daniel



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Weber <daniel.weber@proximabank.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Sonia Petrov <sonia.petrov@proximabank.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 4:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Proxima escalation: 429s after overload protection rollout — request temporary burst exception

Daniel,

Thanks — we’re aligned.

Summary of what we’re implementing (effective Wed Jan 21):
- Scheduled burst exception (ET 09:25–09:50, weekdays)
- us-east
- /v1/chat/completions + /v1/embeddings
- 400 RPS combined ceiling
- Auto-expiry Feb 15
- Rollback triggers: sustained elevated shed rate for your tenant OR enterprise latency risk to protected routes

If you see 429s after Jan 21, please include:
- x-redwood-throttle-reason
- request-id / x-request-id
- Retry-After
and we’ll correlate quickly.

We’ll send a short metrics readout after the first two market opens.

Neha
